extracted.intended_audience: mathematics education researchers; undergraduate mathematics instructors; teacher educators
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and criteria for measuring student mathematical sophistication and van Hiele levels in undergraduate/teacher-preparation settings, including instrument design (MSI), scoring rules (Usiskin van Hiele test), classroom data collection, and analytic coding schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Van Hiele test administration (Usiskin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usiskin’s van Hiele test was administered during the first and last class meetings as a pre- and posttest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer at the start and end of the course so pre/post comparisons are possible; participants in the study typically engaged in inquiry-oriented activities in between (e.g., use of The Geometer’s Sketchpad), which contextualizes interpretation of gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Van Hiele raw scoring (out of 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant was assigned a raw score (out of 25) on Usiskin’s test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 25-item total as a basic quantitative measure alongside level assignment; raw scores can be summarized by group (means, SDs) and compared pre/post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical van Hiele level assignment (4-item criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assign a van Hiele level (n) a participant must answer at least four items correctly at level n and at each preceding level; USiskin groups five questions per VHL (questions 1–5 → VHL 1, 6–10 → VHL 2, etc.). If a participant answers less than four questions correctly at level 1, then level 0 is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called the “4-item criterion” in Usiskin (p.24). The study used this criterion because random guessing was not expected and a higher mastery level was expected given participants' prior HS geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate hierarchical nature with Guttman scalogram analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a Guttman scalogram analysis (similar to Mayberry, 1983) to determine whether the VHLs as tested form a hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scalogram analysis to assess whether the test items operate in a unidimensional hierarchical manner; the study reports the scalogram implied the test operated adequately for hierarchical interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze changes by van Hiele level (focus on high levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret pre/post results not only via raw scores and assigned VHLs but also by examining change at each VHL, especially levels 4 and 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document statistically significant gains (or lack thereof) at particular levels, and consider subgroup analyses (e.g., by gender). Small N at highest levels may limit conclusions about readiness to teach geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizing an activity requires stating actions and ends
rubrics_metrics.description: When characterizing an activity, indicate not only what is being done but also to what end that action is being done (activity = collection of meanings/practices that are goal directed and product of cultural mediation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis of classroom activity should link observable practices to their goals/purposes; this framing guides interpretation of student behavior and emerging meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing and Interpreting Lines in Space (activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: An identified student activity used to construct geometric intuitions, most prevalent when working directly with geometry in R2 and R3; students coordinate lines in space to reach destinations or specify reachable locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for use of directionality, parallelogram rule, scalar multiples, and geometric visualization as evidence of this activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinating Slopes (activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity reflecting use of vectors component-wise and grouping by common ratios (slopes); a slope is an equivalence class of vectors expressible as scalar multiples of one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify when students reason in terms of component ratios and equivalence classes; recognize this reasoning as a precursor to developing meanings for linear dependence and redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating Linear Combinations (activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity where students use scalar multiplication and addition together to identify properties of sets of vectors (e.g., linear dependence/independence, span); language of linear combinations provides a precise, generalized means of communicating possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect transitions from informal/algebraic/geometric reasoning to more formal notation-based descriptions; note that formal meanings emerged as students developed definitions and notation over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom data collection: videotape, student work, reflections, focus groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect whole-class video recordings, small-group episodes, written student work, daily reflections, and conduct focus group interviews chosen to reflect various ability levels and group membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple data sources for triangulation; select focus group participants to represent ability strata and different group memberships; videotape both whole-class and small-group interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-phased analysis procedure (focus groups → coding → cross-check)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase-one: analyze focus group interviews regarding creation/use/interpretation of symbols; Phase-two: code whole-class and small-group episodes with a modified Toulmin scheme to locate meanings functioning-as-if-shared; Phase-three: compare the analyses to create a consistent narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the staged approach to build from interview-based interpretations to coded classroom episodes and then synthesize to ensure consistency across analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified Toulmin coding for classroom argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a modified Toulmin scheme to identify data, claims, warrants/backings that shift roles within argument chains or cease to require justification as they become shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the coding to locate meanings that operate 'as if shared' in the classroom community; focus on how elements of arguments gain or lose justificatory force over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: seeking patterns based on underlying structure
rubrics_metrics.description: One dimension of the MSI construct: seeking to understand patterns based on underlying structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score items or observe behaviors that show students pursue structural pattern-seeking rather than surface features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: making and testing conjectures
rubrics_metrics.description: One MSI dimension: making and testing conjectures about mathematical objects and structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for hypothesis generation and attempts to test or falsify conjectures; value placed on conjecturing is part of the construct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: creating models, examples and non-examples
rubrics_metrics.description: One MSI dimension: creating mental (and physical) models and examples and non-examples of mathematical objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether students construct illustrative examples/non-examples and mental models to support understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: using and valuing precise definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: One MSI dimension: using and valuing precise mathematical definitions of objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for and use of formal definitions should be reflected in item responses or classroom reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: valuing understanding of why relationships make sense
rubrics_metrics.description: One MSI dimension: valuing an understanding of why relationships make sense (seeking conceptual justification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence includes explanations that appeal to underlying reasons rather than rote procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: using and valuing logical arguments and counterexamples
rubrics_metrics.description: One MSI dimension: using and valuing logical arguments and counterexamples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ability and disposition to construct proofs/reasoned arguments and to use counterexamples to refute false claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: using and valuing precise language and distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: One MSI dimension: using and valuing precise language and having distinctions about language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for attention to terminology, careful statements, and sensitivity to linguistic distinctions in mathematical discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication: using and valuing symbolic representations and notation
rubrics_metrics.description: One MSI dimension: using and valuing symbolic representations of, and notation for, objects and ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comfort with symbolic forms as tools for generalization and precise communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Sophistication Instrument (MSI) design and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The MSI is a 25-item, multiple-choice, paper-and-pencil instrument designed to be substantially free of specific mathematics content; items were developed with/consulted by mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring: each MSI item is scored 1 point for the most sophisticated answer (as determined by mathematicians) and 0 for all other options. Use pre/post administration to detect change; instrument intended to capture values/behaviors rather than topical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSI validation: interviews and instructor ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Instrument validation included interviews with 12 stratified students to check that the sophistication reflected in explanations matched item performance, and instructor ratings of student sophistication compared to MSI scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise items based on interview data; compare instructor judgments with student MSI scores as concurrent validity evidence. Report internal consistency (Cronbach alpha) and be attentive to low alpha items.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSI administration and analysis practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Administer MSI at start and end of term across course sections (e.g., Number Systems, Liberal Arts Math, College Algebra); analyze pre/post gains and compare across pedagogical approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When course content overlaps specific items (e.g., graph theory taught in one section), consider deleting those items and reanalyzing. Report group means, standard deviations, and p-values for change; interpret differences in light of pedagogical differences (inquiry-based vs traditional lecture).
